history.heading: Pearling peninsula
paragraphs: Qatar is a small peninsula on the Persian Gulf. It has been inhabited for thousands of years and was part of regional trade networks. For centuries its economy relied on pearl diving, fishing and trade. The fortified town of Al Zubarah, a pearling and trading centre in the 18th and 19th centuries, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The Al Thani family established itself as the ruling family in the mid-19th century, signing a treaty with Britain in 1868. Qatar was under Ottoman influence and then became a British protectorate in 1916.

history.heading: Oil, gas and independence
paragraphs: Oil was discovered in 1939, and exports began in 1949. Qatar became independent on 3 September 1971. In 1995 Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani deposed his father and launched an ambitious modernisation programme, developing natural gas and founding Al Jazeera in 1996. His son, Sheikh Tamim, became emir in 2013.

From 2017 to 2021, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt imposed a blockade on Qatar, accusing it of supporting extremism and ties with Iran. Qatar hosted the FIFA World Cup in 2022, the first in the Arab world.

culture.heading: Society
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language and English is widely used. Qatari citizens are a small minority, about 10–15 percent of residents; most of the population are foreign workers, especially from South Asia. Islam is the state religion, and most citizens are Sunni.
Falconry, camel racing and Arabian horses are traditions. Doha's Museum of Islamic Art and National Museum are landmarks. Machboos is the national dish.

politics.heading: Absolute monarchy
paragraphs: Qatar is an absolute monarchy ruled by the emir. The Shura Council is advisory; its first elections were held in 2021 but were abolished by a 2024 referendum. Political parties are banned. The treatment of migrant workers, especially during the World Cup construction, drew international criticism, leading to labour reforms.
Qatar hosts the largest US military base in the Middle East (Al Udeid) and is an active mediator, including between Israel and Hamas and in Afghanistan.

economy.heading: Gas wealth
paragraphs: Qatar has one of the world's highest incomes per person. It shares the world's largest natural gas field with Iran and is one of the largest exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG), with major expansion under way. The Qatar Investment Authority is one of the largest sovereign wealth funds, owning stakes in companies and landmarks worldwide.
Qatar Airways, finance, tourism and sport are part of its diversification strategy. There is no personal income tax. The Qatari riyal is pegged to the US dollar.
